# Pipedrive
> Pipedrive is the easy, intelligent CRM loved by growing sales teams. It is a cloud-based, sales-first CRM built on the philosophy of Activity-Based Selling — shifting focus from the unpredictable end result (the sale) to the controllable actions (calls, meetings, emails) that drive it. Unlike traditional CRMs that act as passive databases, Pipedrive is built for closing: a proactive productivity tool that uses a visual pipeline, automation and AI to eliminate "rotting" deals and administrative friction. It centralizes the full revenue lifecycle — lead capture, deal management, email and calendar sync, proposals and e-signatures, reporting and forecasting, project delivery and hundreds of integrations — in one workspace that is simple from day one and scales as teams grow. Best fit: B2B, sales-led small and mid-sized businesses (11–250 employees) with a defined sales process and a growing sales team. Key concepts: Pipeline, Stage, Deal, Lead, Activity, Contact (Person), Organization, Insights, Automation, Workflow, Marketplace, Add-on.
## Product
- [Products & features overview](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/products): The full feature set across the sales process.
- [What is CRM](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/crm/fundamentals/what-is-crm): How Pipedrive defines CRM and the problems it solves.
- [Homepage](https://www.pipedrive.com): Core positioning, product tour and free 14-day trial (no credit card required).
- [About Pipedrive](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/about): Company background, awards and newsroom.
## Sales features
- [Sales software (all features)](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/products/sales): Visual, drag-and-drop pipeline and deal management with customizable stages and "rotting" deal alerts.
- [Lead management](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/products/sales/leads): Capture, qualify and organize leads before they enter the pipeline.
- [Email and communications](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/products/sales/email-and-communications): Two-way email sync, open/click tracking, group emailing and a shared sales inbox.
- [Sales automation](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/products/sales/automations): Trigger-based workflows for lead assignment, follow-ups and deal updates.
- [Insights and reports](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/features/insights-and-reports): Visual dashboards for goal tracking, win/loss rates and revenue forecasting.
- [Pulse](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/products/sales-prospecting-software): Real-time, focused prospecting workspace to track follow-ups and surface new opportunities.
- [Onboarding support](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/products/sales/onboarding): Guided setup to get teams started quickly.
## AI-powered features
- [AI CRM (overview)](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/products/ai-crm): Pipedrive's AI capabilities across the sales workflow.
- [AI Sales Assistant](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/features/ai-sales-assistant): Performance nudges and actionable suggestions to keep deals moving.
- [AI email writer](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/products/ai-crm/ai-email-writer): Draft and improve sales emails in seconds.
## Add-ons
- [LeadBooster](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/features/lead-generation-software): Lead generation suite — Chatbot, Live Chat, Web Forms and Prospector (outbound leads from a large GDPR-compliant database).
- [Web Visitors](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/features/web-visitors-add-on): Identify which companies are visiting your website and how they engage.
- [Smart Docs](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/features/smart-docs): Create, share and track proposals and documents from templates, with native e-signatures.
- [Projects](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/crm/resources/crm-project-management): Manage delivery after the deal is won — turn won deals into kanban project boards with tasks and progress tracking.
## Apps & integrations
- [WhatsApp Integration](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/features/crm-for-whatsapp): Pipedrive's WhatsApp Business integration lets sales teams send, receive, and manage WhatsApp conversations directly inside the CRM.
- [Pipedrive Marketplace](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/marketplace): Hundreds of apps and integrations across the revenue lifecycle (e.g. Zapier, Slack, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Gmail/Google Workspace, QuickBooks, Xero, PandaDoc, Mailchimp).
- [About the Marketplace](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/marketplace/about): How integrations map to each stage of the revenue cycle, with guided recommendations.
## Who Pipedrive is for
- **Company profile** — B2B, sales-led SMBs with a defined sales process, a growing sales team and an existing tech stack (typically 6+ business tools); sweet spot ~11–50 employees, scaling toward 51–250.
- **Primary users** — Sales reps, SDRs, Account Executives, Sales Managers, founders/leaders and RevOps/GTM admins.
- **Common industries** — Consulting and agencies, IT and information technology, manufacturing, finance and insurance.
- **Jobs it solves** — (1) Get organized and never miss a follow-up; (2) standardize and optimize the sales process; (3) gain visibility into team performance; (4) orchestrate collaboration across a larger team and connected tools.
## Pricing
- [Pricing plans](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/pricing): Per-seat pricing across four plans — Lite, Growth, Premium and Ultimate — with monthly or annual billing (annual is cheaper per seat). Higher tiers unlock deeper automation, reporting, permissions and support; add-ons are billed separately or bundled into higher tiers. All plans include unlimited contacts and deals, an open API and a 14-day free trial. *Prices are shown in the visitor's local currency and vary by region, so consult the live page for current figures.*

- Compliance posture includes GDPR, SOC 3 and ISO/IEC 27001 (confirm current certifications in the Trust Center).

- [API reference (v1)](https://developers.pipedrive.com/docs/api/v1): RESTful, JSON-based, token-authenticated API available on every plan, with webhooks and official Node.js and PHP clients.
- [Documentation](https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/getting-started): Developer guides and tutorials.
- [Developer community](https://devcommunity.pipedrive.com): Q&A and feedback for builders.

CRM FAQs
What is Pipedrive?
 
Pipedrive is a sales pipeline CRM designed to help small businesses manage leads, track sales activities and close more deals.
How does Pipedrive work?
 
In a nutshell, Pipedrive enables sales teams in small businesses to:
Streamline processes and consolidate sales data in one unified CRM sales tool.
Automate follow-ups and ensure timely responses to leads.
Keep an eye on sales achievements and assess team performance for ongoing improvement.
How to set up Pipedrive?
 
Setting up Pipedrive is straightforward. To get up and running with our CRM 
pipeline management
 tool, here’s a brief guide:
Begin by importing existing data or building your leads database within Pipedrive’s sales CRM software. Explore our Marketplace integrations to infuse your pipeline with even more quality leads.
Define your sales pipeline, create active deals, synchronize your business email and calendar and start scheduling your next activities.
If collaboration is key, set up team access. Pipedrive offers granular permissions, allowing you to fine-tune who can view or modify your CRM data.
As you progress, keep a close eye on your sales outcomes by creating real-time reports and dashboards. This will help you adapt and refine your strategies for even greater success.
How will Pipedrive’s CRM solution help me improve sales?
 
Pipedrive’s CRM sales pipeline makes customer relationship management a breeze by allowing you to track leads, spot opportunities, measure key activities, streamline sales workflows and focus on sales success.
Automated reminders and follow-ups increase your productivity, eliminating repetitive, time-consuming tasks. Real-time reports show your sales reps and sales managers which business processes to prioritize.
Will Pipedrive work for a big team?
 
Yes! Pipedrive’s sales CRM software is well-suited for startups and larger teams alike.
Our pipeline CRM helps large sales and marketing teams streamline their customer interactions. Sales managers and their teams can benefit from a progress tracker, sales automation, procession forecasting, an activity-based planner and top security.
In addition, large teams have access to a dedicated account manager to help them make the most of Pipedrive. Your account manager can also help you onboard other team members to your sales CRM system and guide you on 
pipeline management
 best practices.
What does CRM stand for in sales?
 
“CRM“ in sales stands for “Customer relationship management.” Although the “C” in “CRM” stands for “customer,” the best CRM tools can help teams enhance every stage in the sales cycle.
What is a CRM in sales?
 
A CRM, or sales CRM tool, is a system sales teams use to manage customer data and nurture customer relationships. Several popular CRM and sales tools exist on the market, including Pipedrive.
How does CRM help sales?
 
A CRM for sales enables you and your reps to centralize contact information, track ongoing activities and boost customer retention. Pipedrive’s visual sales pipeline lets you see your entire sales cycle at a glance, highlighting key opportunities. Get notified when you need to follow up, helping you enhance your customer experience and drive more deals than ever.
What is CRM software?
 
CRM software is the technology organizations use to manage relationships and business processes. Typically, CRM software for sales teams lets users track their activities, manage communications with other parties, measure individual and team progress and forecast revenue. The top CRM sales software integrates with other business tools, such as email marketing, document management and website tracking software.
How do I choose a CRM?
 
Choosing a good CRM sales tool for your business requires research and testing. Many companies, including Pipedrive, offer new users a 14-day free CRM trial to see if the software suits their needs. When searching for the best CRM software, consider ease of use, onboarding and results orientation. You should also look for the best pipeline management software and 
sales management software
 to ensure your CRM has all the

Pipedrive products and features FAQs
What are CRM products?
 
CRM products refer to the sales software platform, features belonging to higher tier plans, any other add-ons that give the CRM additional features and Marketplace integrations that sync your CRM data with third-party products.
What features should a CRM have?
 
A good CRM solution allows large and small businesses to easily track their deals, offer a foundation for marketing activities and generate leads for the 
sales pipeline
. It also simplifies document and contract creation, with the flexibility to customize the CRM around the organization’s unique sales processes.
Why are products so important in CRM?
 
Without a good selection of helpful products, a CRM is little better than a spreadsheet.
Businesses that split CRM features into different product plans only need to pay for uses, making a sales cloud CRM system like Pipedrive a more affordable option than on-premises products.
Does Pipedrive have free features and products?
 
Pipedrive offers a 14-day free trial of its plans, and while there isn’t a free version, Pipedrive has done away with arbitrary feature limitations that hinder growth with expensive upgrades.
With over 500 free third-party apps designed to integrate with Pipedrive, you don’t need to pay extra for additional functionality that improves the customer experience, increases profitability and improves retention.

Frequently asked questions
What is CRM pricing and how is it determined? What factors affect CRM software cost?
 
CRM pricing refers to the cost of implementing and using 
customer relationship management software
. The price is determined by factors like number of users, features included in the software, integrations and level of support provided by CRM companies.
How much does a CRM cost on average?
 
CRM costs vary widely depending on the CRM company and features included. On average, the typical cost of CRM software ranges from less than a hundred to several hundred dollars per user per year, with some enterprise-level solutions costing even more. To find the best CRM software prices, research and compare CRM providers based on their pricing plans and features. Pipedrive offers different solutions at price points to match users’ requirements. Learn more on our 
CRM price comparison
 pages.
Can my co-workers join my free trial?
 
Yes, you can invite as many people as you want to join your Pipedrive trial. Simply click on your profile in the top right corner of your screen and select “Add more users” from the drop-down menu.
Will my data be safe?
 
Protecting your business data is one of our highest priorities. Learn more about our rigorous 
security and privacy 
standards.
What is an add-on?
 
Add-ons are additional Pipedrive tools that you can add to any plan.
What’s the difference between annual and monthly billing?
 
The difference is 
how often you pay
 your subscription fee. With monthly billing, you will be charged on the same day each month. With annual billing, you are charged once for the whole year.
Which payment methods do you accept?
 
There are 
different ways
 to pay for Pipedrive including major credit cards, debit cards and PayPal. Your payment options depend on the country you live in.
How can I contact customer support?
 
Our friendly support team is ready to help out. 
Here’s how to get in touch.
What are the prices associated with CRM?
 
As well as the cost of the customer relationship management software itself, which differs based on pricing tier, some providers also charge users for implementation, setup, training, data migration, support and more. You may also be able to purchase credits to get access to more features or more access to the features already on your plan. Try to find a CRM that’s transparent about its pricing. Pipedrive has no hidden costs, making it an excellent choice for anyone with a fixed budget.
What does it cost to implement a CRM?
 
The cost of implementing a CRM varies based on factors such as business size, software choice, user count, customization and integration needs. On-premises setups usually have higher upfront costs. Some CRM providers charge users for implementation. If you choose Pipedrive, implementation is free when you sign up for a pricing plan that’s over $400 a year. Costs differ widely, so a thorough evaluation is essential for an accurate estimate.
